subject: phy
title: Experimental Skills
syllabus: Familiarity with the basic approach and observations of the experiments and activities: vernier callipers and screw gauge; simple pendulum; metre scale; Young's modulus by Searle's method; surface tension by capillary rise; coefficient of viscosity by terminal velocity; specific heat capacity; speed of sound using resonance tube; resistivity using metre bridge; Ohm's law; galvanometer resistance and figure of merit; focal length of mirrors and lenses; refractive index of a glass slab using a travelling microscope; p-n junction and Zener diode characteristics; identification of diode, LED, resistor and capacitor.

body: LC = 1 MSD − 1 VSD = \f{1 MSD}{N}; reading = MSR + VC × LC − zero error
N vernier divisions span N − 1 main divisions, so each vernier division is a little shorter.
Zero error: if the vernier zero sits to the right of the main zero (jaws closed) it is positive; subtract it.
LC = \f{pitch}{circular divisions}; reading = LSR × pitch + CSR × LC − zero error
Zero below the reference line (circular zero has passed) → positive error; above → negative.
Spherometer: measures small heights, hence thickness and radius of curvature R = \f{l^{2}}{6h} + \f{h}{2}.
Pendulum: \f{Δg}{g} = \f{ΔL}{L} + 2\f{ΔT}{T}; timing many swings shrinks ΔT/T.
Products/quotients: keep the fewest significant figures; sums: the fewest decimal places.
Metre bridge: \f{X}{R} = \f{l}{100 − l}; potentiometer: E ∝ balancing length, r = R(\f{l_{1}}{l_{2}} − 1).
A voltmeter across R draws current: V/I gives R ∥ R_{V}, so correct for it.
Ohm's law, Zener and diode characteristics are read from V–I plots (slope = 1/R).

traps: Subtract a positive zero error; add a negative one.
Errors multiply by the power, and ADD even when quantities divide.

pyq.q: Statement I: In a vernier callipers, one vernier scale division is always smaller than one main scale division. Statement II: The vernier constant is given by one main scale division multiplied by the number of vernier scale divisions.
sol: N vernier divisions span N − 1 main divisions, so each vernier division is shorter: I is true.
Vernier constant = 1 MSD − 1 VSD = \f{1 MSD}{N} — divided by N, not multiplied: II is false.
o: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

pyq.q: For an experimental expression y = \f{32.3 × 1125}{27.4}, where all the digits are significant. Then to report the value of y we should write
sol: Multiplication/division: keep the fewest significant figures among the data (3).

pyq.q: Identify the physical quantity that cannot be measured using spherometer :
sol: A spherometer measures small heights (sagitta), so it gives plate thickness and, via R = \f{l^{2}}{6h} + \f{h}{2}, radii of curvature.
Specific rotation needs a polarimeter.
o: Radius of curvature of concave surface
Radius of curvature of convex surface

pyq.q: The measured value of the length of a simple pendulum is 20 cm with 2 mm accuracy. The time for 50 oscillations was measured to be 40 seconds with 1 second resolution. From these measurements, the accuracy in the measurement of acceleration due to gravity is N%. The value of N is:

The total length of potentiometer wire AB is 50 cm. A 6 Ω and a 4 Ω resistor in series are connected across A and B, a galvanometer joins their junction to a jockey P on the wire, and a cell drives the wire. If P is the point where the galvanometer shows zero reading then the length AP is ______ cm.
sol: A Wheatstone bridge: \f{6}{4} = \f{AP}{PB}.

pyq.q: To determine the resistance (R) of a wire, a voltmeter of resistance 10 kΩ is connected across R and a milliammeter measures the total current. The V–I characteristic plotted from the readings passes through (4 V, 2 mA), (6 V, 3 mA) and (8 V, 4 mA). The value of R is ______ Ω.
sol: The milliammeter reads the current through R and the voltmeter together: \f{V}{I} = 2 kΩ = R ∥ 10 kΩ.

pyq.q: Surface tension of two liquids (having same densities), T_{1} and T_{2}, are measured using capillary rise method utilizing two tubes with inner radii of r_{1} and r_{2} where r_{1} > r_{2}. The measured liquid heights in these tubes are h_{1} and h_{2} respectively. [Ignore the weight of the liquid about the lowest point of meniscus]. The heights h_{1} and h_{2} and surfaces tensions T_{1} and T_{2} satisfy the relation:
sol: h = \f{2T cos θ}{ρgr}: the wider tube gives the lower column.
For the same liquid (same T) h_{1} < h_{2}; the measured T comes out equal.

pyq.q: In the experiment for measurement of viscosity 'η' of given liquid with a ball having radius R, consider following statements. A. Graph between terminal velocity V and R will be a parabola. B. The terminal velocities of different diameter balls are constant for a given liquid. C. Measurement of terminal velocity is dependent on the temperature. D. This experiment can be utilized to assess the density of a given liquid. E. If balls are dropped with some initial speed, the value of η will change.
sol: v_{t} = \f{2R^{2}(ρ − σ)g}{9η}: v_{t} ∝ R^{2} (parabola; B false), depends on η (temperature) and on the liquid density σ.
The terminal speed (and so η) does not depend on the starting speed: E false.

pyq.q: Using a simple pendulum experiment g is determined by measuring its time period T. Which plot of \f{1}{T^{2}} against L represents the correct relation?
sol: \f{1}{T^{2}} ∝ \f{1}{L}: a rectangular hyperbola.
o: a curve falling slowly then steeply (concave down)
a straight line falling with L
a curve falling steeply then flattening (a hyperbola)
a curve rising with L, getting steeper

pyq.q: Which of the following resistivity (ρ) versus temperature (T) curves is most suitable to be used in wire bound standard resistors?
sol: A standard resistor must not drift with temperature and should be compact.
Alloys like manganin/constantan: fairly high ρ with an almost zero temperature coefficient — the flat line.
o: a nearly flat line: high ρ that barely changes with T
ρ falling in a straight line with T

pyq.q: A small steel ball is dropped into a long cylinder containing glycerine. Which one of the following is the correct representation of the velocity time graph for the transit of the ball?
sol: Viscous drag grows with speed, so the net force and acceleration shrink.
The speed rises ever more slowly and settles at the terminal velocity.
o: v rises in a straight line and then falls back to zero (a triangle)
v rises quickly at first and levels off at a constant value
v rises in a straight line for ever
v is constant, then falls in a straight line
